name: AudioContext hardware properties
plain: Reads the audio output sample rate, latency and channel count with no prompt.
meaning: Sample rate (44100 or 48000), base and output latency and maximum output channels reveal the audio hardware and OS audio stack, such as wired headphones, Bluetooth or a studio interface.

web.api: new AudioContext(); ctx.sampleRate; baseLatency; outputLatency; destination.maxChannelCount

fields.name: outputLatency
fields.precision: 1 ms or finer, Chrome and Firefox only

limits.headline: Can see your audio setup, such as sample rate and output channels
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads
can: Check the sample rate, usually 44100 or 48000
Check how much delay the audio system has
Count the most speaker channels your device can output
Guess if you use headphones, Bluetooth or built in speakers
cannot: Listen to you or record sound
Name your exact headphones or speakers
Ask you first, since there is no pop up
Play sound without a tap or click on the page in many browsers

story.what_it_is: A page reads your audio output's sample rate, delay and channel count without asking.

marketing.name: AudioContext
marketing.pitch: Represents an audio processing graph and exposes properties like sample rate and output latency.

story.for_you: You never see a prompt. The page learns whether you are on built in speakers, Bluetooth headphones or a studio sound card, just by checking a few numbers.
story.for_makers: Audio apps need these numbers to keep sound in time. The same numbers help fraud and tracking tools tell devices apart, and tell phones from desktops.

use_cases.example: A rhythm game in the browser reads your audio delay and shifts the notes so they match what you hear.
A web piano or synth like Chrome Music Lab picks the best buffer size for your hardware to avoid crackles.
A video call tool sets its sound rate to match your headset so the voice stays clear.
A fraud engine notes that a login came from a device with an unusual sound setup.
A tracking script includes your sample rate in a device ID along with screen size and fonts.
A browser based music studio warns that Bluetooth adds delay, and suggests wired headphones for recording.
A web ear training app measures output delay so it can grade your tapping timing fairly.

technical_bounds: Cannot enumerate devices without mic permission
Autoplay policy may leave context suspended but properties still readable

value.legit_uses: Set buffer sizes for audio apps
